cases.decision: Deliver one bounded reporting pilot or build a platform first?
synthetic_facts: Three fictional buyers report spreadsheet reconciliation work; only one has placed a refundable $300 deposit.
Offer: one monthly report from one supplied export, one revision, no integrations; price $1,200.
Delivery estimate: 8 hours at $75 plus $100 direct cost; $1,000 initial setup; 16 delivery hours available monthly.
cases.baseline_disposition: proceed with one bounded pilot; defer platform
cases.evidence_limit: A refundable deposit is reversible commitment, not proof of retained payment, delivery quality or recurring demand.
cases.next_test: One reviewed pilot; retain actual time, acceptance and final payment; stop expansion if scope or capacity assumptions fail.
cases.provenance: entirely synthetic authored fixture; no actual user or observed transaction

cases.decision: Record a full course because 18 people praised the idea?
synthetic_facts: Eighteen fictional survey responses express interest; no payments or observed completion.
Course: $99 per seat, $9 variable cost, $2,000 fixed preparation cost.
Alternative workshop: six seats maximum, $150 each, $30 variable per seat and $480 fixed preparation/delivery cost.
cases.baseline_disposition: revise to bounded workshop hypothesis; defer full course
cases.evidence_limit: Stated preference is not demand validation; the workshop has no actual buyers.
cases.next_test: Prespecify a paid six-seat workshop with at least four retained paid seats before incurring the stated fixed cost; record cancellation, refund and learning outcomes, not hypothetical sales.
cases.provenance: entirely synthetic authored fixture; no actual user or observed transaction

cases.decision: Scale a subscription because two fictional customers paid?
synthetic_facts: Each requires one hour of support at $100/hour plus $20/month infrastructure.
No demonstrated path reduces support or increases price; operator will not subsidize recurring negative contribution.
cases.evidence_limit: Payment supports willingness to pay at that scope; it does not establish positive contribution or repeatable delivery.
cases.next_test: No expansion or new build. Reopen only with a separately evidenced bounded offer and nonnegative recurring economics; do not assume volume fixes the loss.

cases.decision: Accept custom proofing at the original price?
synthetic_facts: Original product price $45; materials $18, shipping $5, fees $1, labor 0.6 hours at $30.
A fictional customer now asks for three custom proofs, increasing labor to 1.2 hours. No revised price was agreed.
Monthly delivery time after administration is 24 hours; initial photography costs $80; experimental loss cap is $100.
cases.baseline_disposition: revise scope; reject custom proofing at unchanged price
cases.evidence_limit: The original quote cannot validate changed-scope economics; one request is not a market segment.
cases.next_test: Only the original bounded product in a five-order batch, with an explicit maximum $65 modeled setup loss; no custom proofing or implied scale success.

cases.decision: Expand after delivery or inspect the real cost of the first job?
synthetic_facts: A fictional $300 project is paid and accepted; the offer is 3,000 words and one revision.
Estimate was five hours, but the synthetic time log records six including quality review, at $40/hour plus $20 tools.
Setup cost is $160; ten delivery hours remain after administration. The buyer requests another quote but has not repurchased.
cases.baseline_disposition: hold expansion; permit only one capacity-bounded follow-up proposal
cases.evidence_limit: One paid accepted job supports that transaction only; a request for another quote is not renewal or proof of a recurring business.
cases.next_test: One further same-scope job only if authorized; compare delivery/rework time and contribution before increasing commitments.
